newsitem.title: USA: USWC Lt. crudes rise with WTI, but heavies fall.
newsitem.headline: USWC Lt. crudes rise with WTI, but heavies fall.

text.p: U.S. West Coast light crudes were little changed on Tuesday in line with a flat West Texas Intermediate (WTI) market and no trades for Alaskan North Slope (crude), traders said.
With no new ANS deals reported Tuesday, and diffs flat at $1.45 under March WTI, outright prices rose a slight five cents to $22.35/22.55 a barrel.
BP America, a key producer, was asking for $1.25 below March NYMEX, with bidders were as wide as $1.50 a barrel under.
Traders said heavy California grades were flat Tuesday but saw near-term weakeness amid talk Tuesday that Tosco cancelled deliveries of three crude contracts to its Martinez, Calif., refinery.
The company throttled back production at the facility last week after a fire shut its hydrotreater.
Tosco declared force majeure on roughly 40,000 barrels-per-day, a trader said. That left extra crude in a market amply supplied by planned shutdowns at Mobil and Chevron.

California oil companies offered heavy oil at an average price of $18 Tuesday, or $1.50 less a barrel than three weeks ago. Traders reported cargoes sold at 50 to 25 cents under those averages and expected further declines.
Outright prices for Kern River, a representative heavy grade, were offered at $17.75 and bid about $17.50.
